statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 7 sits well below the block threshold because the observed Labor Day price path is two-sided: NQ futures printed 29,682, retraced roughly 117 points back toward the session low and are near 29,565. Stress 61 remains elevated on crude at a six-week high, a 4.77% 10-year yield and the unresolved Strait of Hormuz escalation.
recommendation: The deterministic Tail-to-action mapping yields EA_ON at Tail 7. A narrow evidence-based danger window is published for 22:00-00:00 UTC, covering the CME Globex equity-futures reopen after the five-hour Labor Day halt, when a thin order book would have to absorb the entire holiday information gap. A second, smaller conditional risk cluster is flagged around the 13:30 UTC US cash reopen on 8 September. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures fade a holiday-session high as Hormuz escalation lifts crude to a six-week peak
body: US cash equities, the Nasdaq and the SIFMA bond market are closed for Labor Day, and CME equity index futures trade a shortened session that halts at 17:00 UTC (12:00 CT) before reopening at 22:00 UTC. NQ futures are near 29,565, up about 0.14%, inside a narrow 29,530-29,682 range; the most informative observation of the session is that the move to 29,682 was fully retraced, a completed two-sided sequence rather than one-way extension. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Friday at 29,544.15, up 0.21%, roughly 4% below its 30,762 record. The dominant new information remains geopolitical: US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers over the weekend after Iranian ballistic-missile fire at US warships, and Tehran has declared a restricted maritime zone beyond the Strait of Hormuz. Brent is $97.85 and WTI $92.97, both up about 1.6% and at multi-week highs, with Iran reported to be negotiating a tanker route through the strait with Oman while the US naval blockade continues and the Strategic Petroleum Reserve sits below 290 million barrels, its lowest since 1982. Friday's payrolls printed 162,000 against roughly 53,000 expected with unemployment steady at 4.1%, lifting the 10-year to 4.77% and the 2-year to 4.34% and moving futures-implied odds of a September rate hike to about 60% ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC. Equity volatility is not yet pricing the energy shock, with VIX around 15. Latest-session breadth is rotational rather than directional: semiconductors were uniformly higher on Friday while several megacaps including Apple, Microsoft and Tesla fell, a two-sided tape that historically supports mean reversion. Tail therefore stays low in the absence of observed persistent one-way structure, failed retracements or index extension, while Stress stays elevated on the energy, rates and holiday-liquidity backdrop. The identified discontinuity mechanisms are the thin futures reopen at 22:00 UTC and Tuesday's 13:30 UTC US cash reopen, which must price two sessions of headlines at once; PPI on 10 September and CPI on 11 September are the week's scheduled catalysts, with crude at these levels feeding the inflation channel directly.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the last twenty-four hourly Claude assessments were published; the 21:00 UTC slot on 6 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable. Across the available hours the mapped state held at EA_ON throughout, with Tail between 5 and 9, Stress between 54 and 62 and Confidence between 79 and 86. The dominant mode was normal for twenty-two of the twenty-three published hours, turning mixed only at 14:00 UTC on 7 September as rotational breadth and the approaching futures halt were recognised. The two Tail upticks, to 8 at the 6 September futures reopen and to 9 at 14:00 UTC, both coincided with liquidity transitions rather than with observed directional failure. The published series therefore shows a quiet, range-bound weekend and holiday session with no episode of persistent one-way structure or failed retracement.
outlookSummary: The next twenty-four hours are shaped by market structure more than by scheduled data. Tail is expected to hold near current levels through the last full hour of the shortened futures session, then fall to the run's floor while CME equity index futures are halted between 17:00 and 22:00 UTC, because no price path can form in a closed book. It rises to the highest published level of the run, 16, at the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen, when a thin order book would have to absorb the full holiday information gap alongside Iran's declared Hormuz restricted zone. From there the conditional path normalises through Asian and European hours, with only second-tier US data scheduled, before a second, smaller step up into the 13:30 UTC US cash reopen on 8 September, the first full-liquidity session since Friday. Every one of the twenty-four hours maps to EA_ON: this is conditional gap and headline risk, not observed mean-reversion failure. Stress stays elevated throughout on crude near six-week highs, a hawkish rate backdrop after the 162,000 payrolls print and unusually low outright equity volatility. Confidence eases during the halt, when no live Nasdaq-100 price path is available, and recovers once continuous trading resumes.
